subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Quantum Computing: Beyond Ones and Zeros
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Quantum Computing: Beyond Ones and Zeros.

hook.text: A classical computer tries one path at a time. A quantum computer tries all paths simultaneously.

buildup.text: Quantum bits — qubits — can be 0, 1, or both at once, thanks to a property called superposition.

discovery.text: Google's Sycamore chip solved a problem in 200 seconds that would take a supercomputer 10,000 years.

twist.text: Qubits are incredibly fragile. IBM's quantum chip operates at -273°C, colder than outer space.

climax.text: Quantum computers could break encryption, model new drugs, or simulate entire molecules.

punchline.text: The next revolution runs colder than deep space.

quiz.question: What allows a qubit to process more information than a classical bit?
options: It operates at higher speeds due to superconducting materials
It can exist as 0, 1, or both at once via superposition
It stores data in light pulses instead of electric charges
